key_features.classic_presentation: Ruptured ovarian cyst presents with SUDDEN ONSET SHARP UNILATERAL LOWER ABDOMINAL/PELVIC PAIN that occurs mid-cycle or just before menses. Pain is initially SHARP (7-9/10), then becomes dull/aching over hours as it resolves. Onset is acute, within minutes, often associated with intercourse, exercise, or pelvic exam. Pain IMPROVES OVER 24-48 HOURS (unlike torsion which worsens). Key associated symptoms: Mild nausea, sometimes vaginal spotting, feeling of pressure. Location: Unilateral lower quadrant/adnexal region. Key history: Known ovarian cysts, mid-cycle timing (corpus luteum rupture), reproductive age. Usually BENIGN and SELF-LIMITED. Key positives: Sudden onset, unilateral, improves over hours to days, possible free fluid on ultrasound. Key negatives: Worsening pain suggests torsion not rupture. Hypotension suggests hemorrhagic cyst with significant blood loss (rare).

red_flags: Hypotension or syncope - hemorrhagic cyst with significant blood loss, needs urgent surgery
Severe pain not improving or worsening - consider ovarian torsion instead
Positive pregnancy test - must rule out ectopic pregnancy first
Large amount of free fluid on ultrasound - hemorrhagic cyst, may need intervention
